To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The narrative of the origin of the Lao in contemporary Lao language history books and textbooks has been divided among divergent versions.
the Lao historiographical tradition has undergone a number of transformations over the last two decades.

(a) Lao historiography, like the history of Laos itself, is divided among diverging interpretations, (b) the narrative of the origins and early history of the Lao is divided among three major interpretations, namely: (i) the ‘Ai-Lau’ version, (ii) Marxist-Leninist historiography, and (iii) a return to the ‘roots’, and (c) the most popular reading is that of the ‘Ai-Lou’ version,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changing historiographies of Laos.
the question of how Lao history has been written and what this reveals about the identity of Laos.
the question of how the past is constructed in Laos, how this construction has changed over time, and how it is related to the present.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lao people have a long history and that their identity has been constructed in a variety of ways, but not necessarily in a coherent manner.
the Lao historiography of the early period is in a constant flux, and the future is unpredictable.
the Lao people are not an ethnic group, but a spatial identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lao people’s identity is not only a result of the ‘invention of tradition’ but also of the ‘inventions of history’.
the history of Laos is a history of the Lao identity, and the history of the Lai-Tai identity is a history of a spatial identity.
the Lao narrative is still in a process of formation and that its current state is not a final product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ‘Ai-Lau’ version of the narrative of origins has not yet been challenged by any other interpretation.
the ‘roots’ of Laos are to be found not only in the Lao people’s past, but also in the present and future.
the history of Laos is not a history of a single nation-state, but a history of multiple nations and ethnicities.
